item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Colors observed are red, transparent, orange, blue, green, white, black, violet, yellow, gray, and [REDACTED].

The seeeeeecret special spoop-tastic memetic SPC color, knowledge of this color being so seeeeeeecret and 3spoopy8me that its mere existence is grounds for termination followed by demotion to keter duty and assignment to D-Class assignments.

Wait, the redacted color was moldy cheese green! CONTAINMENT BREACH YO!

Aside from the fact that I can't take this article seriously after censoring a color, the described effect is in no way accurately reflected in the experiment log. If all the atoms of an element in a person's body is changed to another type of atom, it's not going to be "random body part goes spoopy", it'd have an immediate and hardly exciting visual effect on people, almost all of which would end with "Person died when all the nitrogen atoms in their body were replaced with argon, leading to instant death due to chemical reactions"

item.title: Necropost is necro.
item.content:encoded:
We do not employ Josef Mengele.

Or do we?

While I'm here, this is actually one of my favorites. I love chemistry, and cryptochemistry is even cooler (yes, I did make that word up).

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Actually, no. We're not.

Of the +20,000 combinations, most of them would have no effect whatsoever.

For instance, there's no need to see what happens to someone when all the dysprosium in his body (0 atoms / kg) is transformed into lanthanum.

The SCP Foundation is not Unit 731. We do not employ Josef Mengele.

Yes, sometimes our tests kill our test subjects in horribly grotesque ways. But that's not the reason for the tests.

And part of the point of chemistry is a systematization of knowledge. The hydrogen=>helium test was useful, and now we know exactly what will happen for hydrogen=>neon, hydrogen=>argon, hydrogen=>krypton, etc.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Yeah, see….the human body is pretty much dependent on being made up exactly of what it's usually made up of. The removal of any element will cause the human body a great deal of distress. Especially since a great many of the basic elements of life aren't 'pure'. If all the oxygen is transformed into nitrogen, there goes all of the oxygenated blood, all of the water, etc. Every chemical in the body with an 'O' is changed to 'N'. There are no 'benign' elemental swaps.

I rarely mark down, but this deserves it. It fails on a basic scientific level, in a way that is completely ludicrous. Yes, even more ludicrous than the living statues, the evil gearbox, and the time-displaced city.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Hmmm. Weird… So, you eat a couple pills, and all the zinc in your body might turn to argon? I admit I don't know much about the chemistry of human anatomy, but it sounds to me like eating these pills would simply kill someone most of the time, especially if the element selected for change happens to be carbon, or oxygen. So, I'm a bit confused by the addendum; what possible molecular swap could there be that would actually be healthy? And why would you be giving most-likely-fatal SCP-pills to 191 anyhow?
